newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says to clear deal on sale of Britannia gas.
newsitem.headline: EU says to clear deal on sale of Britannia gas.

text.p: The European Commission said on Monday it planned to clear an agreement between eight European and U.S. oil and gas companies on the sale of gas from the Britannia gas condensate field.

The agreement linked Chevron Corp's and Texaco Inc's British subsidiaries, Amerada Hess Ltd, Conoco Ltd and Conoco Petroleum Ltd, both part of the DuPont group, Phillips Petroleum Company's British unit, and Britain's Santa Fe Exploration Ltd and Union Texas Britannia Ltd.

It consisted of an oral accord, between February 1992 and the end of 1994, to appoint one of the member companies to be responsible for the conduct of negotiations with potential gas buyers, the Commission said in a statement published in the EU's Official Journal.
The Britannia field is found in the central area of the United Kingdom's continental shelf.
The Commission said that sales were concluded between July 1994 and December 1994 for delivery from 1998.

It said that with regard to sales to the British market "no potential Continental competitor to Britannia could have existed...as there was then no means of transporting such gas". It also invoked the lack of infrastructure to transport the gas to Continental markets as a further reason to clear the agreement.
The Commission called on interested parties to give their views on the agreement, which the partners submitted for EU clearance in January 1995, before taking a decision.
